title: 1955 AHSME Problem 38
statement: Four positive integers are given. Select any three of these integers, find their arithmetic average, and add this result to the fourth integer. Thus the numbers \(29,\) \(23,\) \(21\) and \(17\) are obtained. One of the original integers is:

solutions.text:
If the original integers sum to \(S,\) the result associated with singled-out integer \(x\) is \[ x+\frac{S-x}{3}=\frac{S+2x}{3}. \] Summing all four reported results counts the total as \(2S,\) so \[ S=\frac{29+23+21+17}{2}=45. \] The result \(29\) therefore comes from \(x=\dfrac{3(29)-45}{2}=21.\)

Thus, one original integer is \(21,\) and the correct answer is B.
hints: If the original sum is \(S\) and the singled-out integer is \(x,\) the result is \(\frac{S+2x}{3}\)
Sum all four reported results to determine \(S\)
